questions.q: The page number and word count of the open document are shown on the —
questions.solution: The **status bar** at the bottom shows Page x of y, the live word count, language and the zoom slider.

questions.q: A full mesh of 8 computers needs how many links?
questions.solution: 8x7/2 = **28**. 56 skips the halving; 64 is 8 squared.

questions.q: To select the **entire worksheet** at once, press —
questions.solution: **Ctrl+A** selects all; one press covers the sheet (a second press extends it in older versions).

questions.q: The total number of cells in one Excel 2016 worksheet is —
questions.solution: 16,384 columns multiplied by 1,048,576 rows = **17,179,869,184 cells** (about 17.18 billion).

questions.q:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

Sita said to Gita, "You are late for the class."
options: Sita told Gita that she is late for the class.
Sita told Gita that she was late for the class.
Sita told Gita that you were late for the class.
Sita told Gita that they were late for the class.
questions.solution: you is the listener, so it becomes **she** (Gita); are steps to **was**. 'She is late' skips the rung; keeping 'you' leaves the quote half-direct; 'they' breaks the number — one listener, singular.
questions.shortcut: 2nd person borrows the listener: you → she/he.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

A black sheep
options: a member who brings disgrace to the family or group
the youngest child in a family
questions.solution: Black = disgrace. *A black sheep* is the member whose conduct shames the family or group.

questions.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.  I found ___ one-rupee coin on the pavement.
questions.solution: 'One' begins with the consonant sound 'wu' → **a** one-rupee coin.

questions.q: If the scheme described in the second paragraph spreads widely, which of the following is most likely to happen?
options: Farmers will stop growing crops altogether
Less groundwater will be pumped out, since spare power can earn money instead
Power companies will stop buying electricity from farmers
Diesel pumps will become popular again
questions.solution: The scheme lets farmers sell spare electricity 'instead of using it to pump more water'. If many farmers join, less extra pumping will happen, so less groundwater will be drawn. Nothing suggests farmers stop farming; the scheme is the power company buying electricity, so it stopping is the opposite; there is no reason to return to paid diesel.
questions.shortcut: State the passage's rule (spare power → money, not pumping) and apply it to 'many farmers'.
questions.passage:
When Harish replaced his diesel pump with a solar one, his monthly fuel bill fell to zero. For the first time, he could water his fields in the afternoon without worrying about cost, and he did — often for longer than the crop needed. Two years later, the water in his borewell had dropped by several metres.

His neighbours noticed. Some of them have now joined a scheme under which farmers can sell spare solar electricity to the power company instead of using it to pump more water. Harish says the payment is small but steady. 'Earlier, extra sunshine meant extra pumping,' he says. 'Now it means extra money.'

questions.q: Which allotrope of carbon **conducts electricity**?
questions.solution: **Graphite** has free electrons between its layers — used as electrodes. Diamond is an insulator despite being the hardest substance.

questions.q: **Servants of India Society** (1905), which trained dedicated public workers, was founded by —
questions.solution: **Gokhale** founded the Servants of India Society in 1905 — he was also Gandhi's acknowledged political guru.

questions.q: Which single European river flows through the greatest number of capital cities?
questions.solution: The **Danube** passes through **Vienna (Austria), Bratislava (Slovakia), Budapest (Hungary) and Belgrade (Serbia)** - four capitals; the Volga is Europe's longest river but has no capital on it.

questions.q: **Gitanjali**, for which its author received the Nobel Prize for Literature in 1913, is a collection of —
questions.solution: **Gitanjali** ('Song Offerings') is Tagore's collection of poems; he was the **first Asian** to win a Nobel Prize.

questions.q: In a group of 500 people, the number who like only tea is twice the number who like only coffee. If 90 people like both and 50 like neither, how many people like coffee?
questions.solution:
Only tea $+$ only coffee $= 500 - 90 - 50 = 360$.
Only coffee $= 360 \div 3 = 120$.
Coffee $= 120 + 90 = 210$.

questions.q: If 3 men or 5 women can complete a piece of work in 12 days, then 6 men and 5 women together will complete it in:
In what ratio should a 25% acid solution be mixed with a 50% acid solution to obtain a 40% acid solution?
questions.shortcut: Cross the distances from the mean 40 ⇒ 2 : 3.

questions.q: A set has 7 elements. How many subsets does it have?
questions.solution: Number of subsets $= 2^n = 2^7 = 128$.
questions.shortcut: Powers of two: 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128 — the seventh doubling is 128.

questions.q: If **dog is called cat**, **cat is called rat**, **rat is called lion**, and **lion is called cow**, which animal catches mice?
questions.solution: A real **cat** catches mice. Cat is called **rat**. Answer: Rat. (Cat is only the new name of a dog.)

questions.q:
**Statements:** All shirts are cotton.

**Conclusions:**
I. All shirts are white.
II. Some shirts are not white.

Which of the conclusions follow(s)?
options: Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.solution: Nothing links shirts with white, so neither follows alone; the pair is a true negation pair. **Either I or II follows.**
questions.shortcut: The statements may ignore the pair completely — the pair rule still works.

questions.q: In a certain code, **HIDE is written as SRWV**. How is **GOAT** written in that code?
questions.solution: H(8)+S(19) = 27, I(9)+R(18) = 27 — **opposite letters**. G↔T, O↔L, A↔Z, T↔G → **TLZG**.
questions.shortcut: 27-sum check, then the opposite-pairs table does the whole question.

questions.q: In a code language, **'blue sky' is written 'ta pa'** and **'sky walk' is written 'pa sa'**. What is the code for **'blue'**?
questions.solution: 'sky' is common to both sentences and 'pa' is the common code → sky = pa. In sentence 1 the leftover word 'blue' takes the leftover code **ta**.
questions.shortcut: Common word ↔ common code; leftovers pair up.
